_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy.

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-comparator-controlled
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind trial with placebo (n=174), guselkumab 100 mg SC (n=329), and adalimumab (n=333) arms; placebo crossed over to guselkumab at Week 16.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (PASI ≥12, PGA ≥3, BSA ≥10%) who were candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 16: proportion achieving IGA of cleared (0) or minimal (1), and proportion achieving PASI 90 (guselkumab vs placebo).
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0/1 at Week 16: 85% guselkumab vs 7% placebo; PASI 90: 73% vs 3% (p<0.001).

pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-comparator-controlled with randomized withdrawal and retreatment
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind trial with placebo (n=248), guselkumab 100 mg (n=494), and adalimumab (n=248) arms, with randomized withdrawal/retreatment based on PASI 90 response.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults ≥18 years with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (PASI ≥12, PGA ≥3, BSA ≥10%) who were candidates for phototherapy or systemic therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 16: proportion achieving IGA of cleared (0) or minimal (1), and proportion achieving PASI 90 (guselkumab vs placebo).
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0/1 at Week 16: 84% guselkumab vs 8% placebo; PASI 90: 70% vs 2% (p<0.001).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥1%): upper respiratory infections, headache, injection site reactions, arthralgia, diarrhea, gastroenteritis, tinea and herpes simplex infections. Infections occurred in 23% of TREMFYA subjects vs 21% placebo through 16 weeks. Upper respiratory infections 14.3% (TREMFYA) vs 12.8% (placebo).
target_moa: Guselkumab is a human IgG1λ monoclonal antibody that selectively binds the p19 subunit of IL-23 and blocks its interaction with the IL-23 receptor, reducing downstream production of IL-17A.

rems.type: A Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) is not needed.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues unexpected for a biologic of this class.

requirement.text: 3225-1: Conduct a PK, safety and efficacy study in pediatric subjects 6 to less than 18 years of age with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (deferred pediatric study under PREA).

requirement.text: 3225-2: A prospective, registry-based observational exposure cohort study comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to guselkumab during pregnancy to an unexposed control population.

citations.quote: 3225-2 A prospective, registry-based observational exposure cohort study that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to guselkumab during pregnancy to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: 3225-3: Conduct a retrospective cohort study (or case-control study) to assess adverse pregnancy outcomes in women exposed to guselkumab during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.

citations.quote: 3225-3 Conduct a retrospective cohort study using claims or electronic medical record data or a case control study to assess adverse pregnancy outcomes such as major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, small for gestational age, neonatal deaths, and infant infections in women exposed to guselkumab during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.

requirement.text: 3225-4: Conduct an observational study to assess the long-term safety of guselkumab compared to other therapies, with primary outcome of long-term risk of malignancy.
